Is this data structure shared outside of this dissector?  If not, just make it part of the c file.

Yes, this data is passed to the upper level dissector [here](https://gitlab.com/dmitrmax/wireshark/-/blob/nats/epan/dissectors/packet-nats.c#L403).

NATS doesn't impose any format for the payload, so there can be the upper level dissector which may need some info to determine how to dissect the payload. This info is shared within this structure.
Can you attach some pcap ? do you have fuzz the code ?
No, I didn't fuzz the code. Is there any framework for it in Wireshark. I'll look for the pcap a bit later.

You can go to your build folder and run something like

VALGRIND=1 ~/wireshark/tools/fuzz-test.sh ~/captures/*

I did some fuzzing for a couple of hours. It took 17500 rounds and everything is fine so far.

Unfortunately, I can't publish these pcaps as they might have sensitive data. I'll try to generate some pcaps from the NATS examples tomorrow.

AFAIU, the project's code style imposes variable declaration at the start of a block. I just wanted to bring the variables which are needed only in this part code closer to their usage. Is this not encouraged?
yes, it is better to declare variable on top of function
Ok, fixed
Not needed.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22226/diffs?diff_id=1560953764&start_sha=c7b9ef5813d421d71888ad7fc5a587cae2ede6fd#115ca360cc45bd29a214c8c4f0bd83c9114c8a3d_23_23)
Ah! My bad. It was previously a plugin. Fixed
Can offset or length be -ve?  Use an unsigned type instead?  Or are you usefully using -1 as a special value?

I'm really keen on the idea of offsets and lengths being size_t (or just unsigned). But the entire Wireshark API (especially tvb_* functions) is built around the offsets and (partially) lengths are being signed integers. So, I'm just trying to follow the style.

If you insist I can make them unsigned.
That's fine.

Your blurb/long-text here is just the protocol name + the label, so not really adding any info.  In this case, you could just leave it as NULL - when you click on a protocol field the label shows in the bottom-left corner of the screen, and the protocol name will be visible too.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22226/diffs?diff_id=1560953764&start_sha=c7b9ef5813d421d71888ad7fc5a587cae2ede6fd#115ca360cc45bd29a214c8c4f0bd83c9114c8a3d_885_884)
Legit. Made more "wordy" descriptions here and for nats.subscription.max_msgs.
Please check the other items - there are definitely some where you still just have the blurb set to "NATS + <label>"
I've revised all of them and corrected many of them to NULL but for others gave meaningful blurb
Would any sub-dissectors registering in "nats.subject" need this type?
Yes. Pretty much. Because the way the sub-dissector dissects payload can depend either on subject or on headers or both.
You are not yet looking up entries in this table?  Maybe at least add a comment to nats_dissector_search() about how this will be used later?

Actually I do look them up, but right now the dissector searches only ">" entry which is a special wildcard in NATS to much all the subjects. And there is a comment about that. One day this would be a way to subscribe sub-dissector only to selected subjects.
I misunderstood, ok - was looking for refs to that table variable, but see that you do a (linear?) search of the entries in the table, accessed by name.

Yes, because the idea was to implement something like NATS subscriptions work. For example, I can bind the sub-dissector to `MyService.*.Get` subject in order to dissect all PDUs for that wildcard subject (and replies from it). This makes a simple (but O(1)) index into the hash table meaningless: `MyService.Table.Get` should be dissected but the hashtable lookup won't match this key with `MyService.*.Get`. 

But to do it effective without searching and matching the dissector for every PDU, I need to built some tree-like structure. And this structure should be rebuilt every time when the dissectors table is changed. I don't see any hooks for this though. That is why I have postponed the implementation of this feature for now.

That's ok too - shouldn't delay this MR.

Maybe you could have a 2-stage lookup.  A fast hashtable, but for entries that aren't cached yet, use GRegex (and cache the answers) ?  Something like that.
Just use char rather than gchar - we are trying to move away from glib types.
This could be a `const uint8_t *`, and drop the typecast.
